title: Interfaces (Implicit Satisfaction)
desc: If a struct has all the methods an interface declares, it implements it automatically — no implements keyword. This is how the engine injects mock dependencies in tests.

title: Goroutines vs async/await
desc: Goroutines are cheap green threads multiplexed across OS cores. traCtl uses them to run workflow steps truly in parallel — not cooperatively like Node.js event loop.

title: sync.RWMutex
desc: Protects shared maps (stepResults, vars) from concurrent goroutine races. RLock() allows many simultaneous readers. Lock() is exclusive write access.

title: embed.FS — Binary Includes Files
desc: The compiled binary includes the entire dist/ folder baked in via //go:embed directive. Deploy a single file — no external assets needed.

title: context.Context
desc: Passed as first arg to every async function. Carries cancellation signals and deadlines. When a parent timeout fires, all child operations cancel automatically via the same context.

title: Channels as Semaphores
desc: A buffered channel of size N acts as a semaphore — only N goroutines can hold a slot simultaneously. traCtl uses this to cap concurrent script executions.

title: Error Handling (No throw)
desc: Go functions return (value, error). You check every error explicitly — there's no try/catch. golangci-lint fails the build if you ignore an error.

title: Struct Tags (JSON/YAML)
desc: Backtick annotations on struct fields control JSON/YAML key names and omitempty behaviour. Like @JsonProperty in Java or @Expose in class-transformer.

title: Dependency Injection via Interfaces
desc: engine.Config has optional fields Planner, Compiler, Evaluator. In tests inject mocks; in production leave nil (defaults used). No DI framework needed.

title: syscall/js (WASM Bridge)
desc: Go code compiled to WASM registers JavaScript-callable functions via js.Global().Set(). The bridge file makes Go engine functions available as window.tractl.* globals.

title: Build Injection via -ldflags
desc: goreleaser injects Version, Commit, BuildTime into the binary at link time. No config file or env var at runtime — the value is baked into the binary.

title: Topological Sort (DAG)
desc: Step ordering uses DFS-based topological sort on dependsOn edges. Steps with no edges between them form a 'wave' and run in parallel. Cycle = validation error.
